question: Looking back at your completed task, how did you decide what to read or request next, and when you had enough information to answer? Give a brief account of observable choices and the information you expected further reads to provide.
answer: I made the required first request for the library-literal HAL resource. Its embedded CLI binding explained the general package-query gesture but only described that facet, so I followed its bindings href to find the exposed dependency facets. From those returned hrefs, I requested depends to determine exact matching and edge-depth behavior, dependency-depth for legal values and requirements, dependency-target for the TFM and all rule, and depends-transitive to check whether it was the preferred predicate or had different matching semantics. I stopped once those responses supplied the command syntax, depth and target restrictions, candidate limit, and the distinction between preferred exact depends and the legacy transitive term. More reads would have been verification rather than filling a task-critical gap; I did not run an inspection, so actual package results remained unknown.
